label: Быть
description: A full deck for irregular быть: zero present, the был/была/было/были past, the буду…будут future, есть for existence, and the imperative будь.

missions.phrase: Вчера весь день я был дома.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Past tense. 1. 'Был' is the masculine past form, agreeing with a male speaker. 2. 'Вчера весь день' frames the duration. 3. Russian past tracks gender, not person.

missions.phrase: Утром ты была очень занята.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Feminine past tense. 1. 'Была' is the feminine past, agreeing with a female 'ты'. 2. 'Занята' is the short feminine adjective 'busy'. 3. Past быть agrees in gender, never person.

missions.phrase: К вечеру он будет полностью готов.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Future form. 1. 'Будет' is the irregular 3sg future stem. 2. 'Полностью готов' gives the resulting state. 3. The future conjugates by person, unlike the silent present.

missions.phrase: Прошлым летом мы были там.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Plural past tense. 1. 'Были' is the plural past form for any-gender group. 2. 'Прошлым летом' anchors the time. 3. The plural past ignores both gender and person.

missions.phrase: Завтра вы будете готовы к экзамену.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Polite/plural future. 1. 'Будете' is the 2pl/formal future form. 2. 'Готовы к экзамену' keeps the outcome concrete. 3. Future быть conjugates by person and number.

missions.phrase: Через час они будут здесь.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Third-person plural future. 1. 'Будут' is the 3pl future, closing the irregular scaffold. 2. 'Через час' sets the timeframe. 3. Future быть uses real conjugation throughout.

missions.phrase: Сейчас я дома и совсем один.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Zero present. 1. There is NO present-tense form of быть in modern Russian. 2. You simply say 'я дома', dropping the verb entirely. 3. The link between subject and predicate stays silent.

missions.phrase: Она была очень рада нашей встрече.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Feminine past. 1. 'Была' is end-stressed (была́) and marks a female subject. 2. 'Рада' is the short feminine adjective 'glad'. 3. Russian past agrees in gender, not person.

missions.phrase: Для всех нас это было очень важно.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Neuter past. 1. 'Было' is the neuter past form, agreeing with 'это'. 2. 'Важно' is the neuter short adjective 'important'. 3. Past tense tracks the subject's gender, never the speaker's person.

missions.phrase: Всё это было уже очень давно.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Neuter past. 1. 'Было' agrees with neuter 'это'. 2. 'Давно' means 'long ago'. 3. With impersonal 'это' the verb defaults to the neuter past form.

missions.phrase: Я буду очень рад тебя видеть.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: First-person future. 1. 'Буду' is the irregular 1sg future of быть. 2. 'Рад' is the masculine short adjective 'glad'. 3. The future uses real conjugation, unlike the zero present.

missions.phrase: Сегодня вечером ты будешь дома?
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Second-person future. 1. 'Будешь' is the 2sg future form. 2. 'Сегодня вечером' sets the time. 3. Future быть conjugates by person, contrasting with the empty present.

missions.phrase: Мы всегда будем рады вашим гостям.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: First-person plural future. 1. 'Будем' is the 1pl future form. 2. 'Рады' is the plural short adjective 'glad'. 3. This is a warm, reusable hospitality frame.

missions.phrase: Сегодня у меня есть свободное время.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Existence and possession. 1. 'Есть' is the only surviving present form, used for 'there is / I have'. 2. 'У меня есть' is the standard possession frame. 3. Outside existence, present быть stays silent.

missions.phrase: Здесь рядом есть чистая вода.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Existence есть. 1. 'Есть' asserts that something exists here. 2. 'Здесь рядом есть' means 'here nearby there is'. 3. This is the present быть's one surviving form.

missions.phrase: Всегда будь готов к этому.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Imperative. 1. 'Будь' is the singular informal imperative of быть. 2. 'Готов' is the masculine short adjective 'ready'. 3. Imperative быть commands a future state.

missions.phrase: Будьте здоровы и берегите себя.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Polite imperative. 1. 'Будьте' is the plural/formal imperative of быть. 2. 'Здоровы' means 'healthy'; the phrase is a common toast. 3. Use 'будьте' for politeness or groups.

missions.phrase: Я никогда не был там раньше.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Negated past. 1. 'Не был' negates the masculine past form. 2. 'Там раньше' marks the place not visited. 3. Negation precedes the verb; gender agreement still holds.

missions.phrase: Его не будет в офисе завтра.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Negated future. 1. 'Не будет' negates the 3sg future. 2. With negation the subject goes genitive ('его'), an impersonal absence. 3. 'Завтра' sets the time.

missions.phrase: Вчера вечером они были дома.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Plural past. 1. 'Были' is the plural past form for any-gender group. 2. 'Вчера вечером' anchors the time. 3. The plural past ignores both gender and person.

missions.phrase: На этой неделе вы будете заняты.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Polite/plural future. 1. 'Будете' is the 2pl/formal future form. 2. 'Заняты' is the plural short adjective 'busy'. 3. A clean frame for scheduling and instruction.
